data.summary: Gate bug in the shared xtask: gate --branch can leave an old commit's xtask in the caller's target dir, and the next gate run is a silent pass
data.body: Found while porting xtask (our branch worktree-agent-a877a9cd7259eb95c). gate --branch builds each older commit in the caller's CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Afterwards, `cargo xtask` in the same worktree ran the first commit's empty xtask stub: exit 0, no output, so a second gate run looked like a pass. Your gate handles the target dir the same way, as far as we can see. Suggested fix: build each commit under its own target dir (or one keyed by commit), and have gate refuse a binary built from a commit that isn't HEAD. We haven't changed it here, since VectorCraft holds the master copy; our workaround is running gate from a separate xtask build.

data.summary: VC verify has two fail-open paths our review found: dofile matched as literal text, and an unreadable oracle/ read as no fixtures
data.body: Codex found both in our port of your xtask verify. Our fix is b698dcb (branch worktree-agent-a877a9cd7259eb95c, under review), and we read your main efa66b4 for the same code. 1. map_deps (xtask/src/verify.rs ~3197) looks for the literal `dofile(`, so `dofile ("x.lua")`, a comment before the parenthesis, or a call with no parentheses loads a map whose hash the manifest needn't list; loadfile and require aren't seen at all. Ours now reads the map as Lua tokens and refuses loadfile, require, load, loadstring, any other use of the name dofile, and computed paths. 2. The stray-trace scan in check_games (~3698) is `if let Ok(fs::read_dir(..))` plus `.flatten()`: an unreadable oracle/ skips the scan and per-entry errors are dropped. load_fixture_manifests (~3560) also drops entry errors, and research.rs check (~127) and check_game (~150) treat an unreadable oracle/ as no fixtures. Ours lets only NotFound mean no fixtures. Regressions in b698dcb: every_spelling_of_dofile_is_followed, loading_forms_verify_cant_follow_are_refused, an_unreadable_oracle_directory_fails. Take them once it lands, or ask for the diff.

Both pieces are ported on branch `port-gate-host`: the build host and the scratch-worktree sweep. The tip, 81f8d03, passes `cargo xtask gate --branch` and its branch review approves it. The first review (of db45a34) found one high-severity problem; it is fixed in the last commit. Nothing is landed or pushed, and main is still 666b30f, so no rebase was needed.

Worktree: `/Users/jamess/GitHub/avoidmissingball/.claude/worktrees/agent-port-gate-host`.

## Commits (666b30f..81f8d03)
1. **8c331c4** Stamp version 3: adds the gating xtask's source hash, the `host` name and the `xtask-commit` lines. Versions 1 and 2 still read. A stamp that names a host is trusted only if its xtask was built from the tip and its source hash matches the tip's files as git holds them. It reuses the existing `srchash.rs` rather than adding a second copy.
2. **31c6242** The build host: `xtask/src/gate_host.rs`, `tools/gate-host`, and `--host` on `gate --branch` and `land`.
   - **Off by default:** a host runs only when `~/.config/avoidmissingball/gate-host` names it. With no file, or a different host, it errors and runs nothing; no flag or `local` gates on this Mac. No agent writes that file, and the call is recorded in `docs/decisions.md`.
   - **Tests:** they use a fake ssh and cargo; nothing contacts a real host. The "Connection to bytecut closed" and "blackhole" lines in the test output are printed by that fake ssh.
3. **61400d6** The sweep: `xtask/src/gate_scratch.rs`, mounted as `gate::scratch`, plus `gate --sweep [--dry-run]`.
   - **Locking:** each scratch tree is created locked with its gate's pid and start time, and a watchdog removes it when the gate dies.
   - **Sweeping:** each new scratch sweeps trees whose gate is dead.
   - **Removal fallback:** it now deletes only the tree's own git entry, where it used to run a repo-wide prune.
   - **Kept:** our mkdir-plus-counter naming (`claim_dir`).
4. **db45a34** Docs:
   - `docs/sync.md`: the VectorCraft commits taken (main 571fc244: `gate_host.rs` and `tools/gate-host` at 9a4573a4, `gate_scratch.rs` at 398575d5, gate.rs at 8625a18a).
   - `docs/decisions.md`: four delegated calls, with the two earlier "left out" rows marked as replaced.
   - `docs/tech-reference.md`: the lookup findings.
   - The new prose went through `/avoid-ai-writing`. That pass was model-only: its detector and checker scripts did not run.
5. **81f8d03** Review fix. `tools/gate-host` ran `git worktree prune` across the whole host repository after every run. That could drop another worktree's entry and leave a commit only it held open to garbage collection. It now removes only its own run's entry. The new test failed on db45a34 with "the other tree's entry was pruned".

## Failure cases covered by tests
Every new test fails on 666b30f; the commit messages say how.
- **Gates that die:** killed by KILL, TERM, INT or HUP, including when the parent had those signals ignored. A child process still working in the tree keeps it until that child exits.
- **Zombies and pid reuse:** `ps` tells a gone, zombie or running owner apart, and a reused pid is caught by the start time, read the same under any time zone.
- **Refusals:**
  - a live process in the tree, or `lsof` failing;
  - a branch checked out;
  - changed, untracked or ignored files, each named in the reason;
  - a lock that changed while the sweep ran;
  - `ps` failing.
- **Unsaved commits:** a dead tree's commit that only a side branch holds is archived under `refs/archive/amb-gate/` before removal, both by the sweep and by the watchdog.
- **Failed removals:** the fallback leaves other trees' entries alone, a deleted tree whose HEAD can't be read keeps its entry, and a failed `worktree add` cleans up its directory (or reports why it couldn't).
- **Races:** two scratches created in the same instant get different paths.
- **Host:** a lost connection reattaches, a host lost for good cleans itself up, a forged or mismatched host stamp is not trusted, and a host run leaves other worktrees alone.

## Left out
`--ci`, the bounded idle wait, `check_this_build` and `hold_target`: neither the host nor the sweep needs them. Because `check_this_build` is missing, a build with no valid source hash writes no `xtask` line in its stamp. The caffeinate wake lock was taken, since a sleeping Mac cut the host's ssh connections; it covers host gates only.

## To copy to the other projects
- **VectorCraft** should take four changes:
  - the host stays off until an owner config names it;
  - a dead tree's HEAD counts as saved only on main or an archive ref (VectorCraft accepts any ref, so a feature branch deleted after landing loses the commit);
  - a kept tree's reason names every path a removal would lose, not just the first;
  - the targeted cleanup in `tools/gate-host`, which has the same repo-wide prune.
  
  Smaller: `Stamp::by` skips an invalid hash.
- **BewareILive** has none of this: no host, stamp v3 or sweep.

| `/git/htmldocs` | how `for-each-ref --contains` matches patterns, and `status --ignored` output | Drove the main-or-archive check (checked on a throwaway repo) and the ignored-file listing |
| `/websites/doc_rust-lang_stable_std` | `process_group(0)` and how kill, wait and try_wait reap | Confirmed the watchdog and wake-lock code |
| `/openssh/openssh-portable` | exit code 255, keepalive timing, `BatchMode` | Confirmed reattaching on 255 |

Phase A and phase C of #18 are done on branch `pokey-sound`. Phase B (our own recreation of a sound) has not started. The tip is `b6e5287`: Codex approved it after three review rounds, and `gate --branch --host studio` passed. Nothing is landed or pushed.

**What a player gets:** in live play, the shot sound now plays through the speakers. It is the original, recorded from MAME and played as a marked placeholder. The death sound is wired too, but it can't fire in live play yet, because the core only gets a death fed from a trace.

**Commits** (worktree `.claude/worktrees/agent-pokey-sound`, base `d4b8eeb`):
- `fc01463`: `mame/sound.lua` (ported from BewareILive 4fc22aef), `cargo xtask sound-record`, a sound check inside `cargo xtask verify`, the manifest, three placeholders and their replays.
- `cc7728a`: the game plays sound through cpal. It loads the clips, resamples each once to the device's rate and mixes them in the device callback. The cues read the core's state after each step and never change it. Also `docs/games/centiped/sound.md` and the mechanics rows.
- `39eb5d1`: docs (decisions, sync, oracle section 10, tech-reference, gaps, devlog). The `/avoid-ai-writing` pass is done.
- `d087065`, `594bfff`, `b6e5287`: fixes for review findings, each with a regression test shown failing first:
  - `sound-record` now writes clips and manifest as one transaction, with backups and rollback.
  - The manifest's frame-window check no longer overflows on extreme numbers; before, it could crash the game at startup.
  - Recording takes the same repository lock as `verify --regen`.
  - Backups are kept if a restore fails.
  - The queue of sound requests is capped at 64, and nothing more is sent once the device is lost.

**Sounds recorded** (MAME 0.289 `centiped3`, 192 kHz, mono 16-bit, under `assets/original/centiped/`):

| Sound | Replay | Frames | Samples | Bytes | Plays in game |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shot | `replays/centiped3/sound-shot.txt` (bot-waves, first 1200 frames) | 1185 to 1198 | 41,600 | 83,244 | yes, when the shot starts to fly |
| death | `replays/centiped3/sound-death.txt` (wave1-idle, first 530 frames) | 466 to 524 | 185,600 | 371,244 | wired; only fires once death is built |
| march | `replays/centiped3/sound-march.txt` (move-fire, first 20 frames) | 0 to 16 | 51,200 | 102,444 | no; the core has no centipede yet |

Each clip matched the same window of a full-replay recording. A run through `sound.lua` gave the stored move-fire trace byte for byte. No run wrote RAM or touched the sound chip.

**Measured** (all in `sound.md`):
- **Shot:** starts the frame after the shot leaves and lasts 11 frames. It is a pulse train whose pitch falls from about 4.4 kHz to 1.5 kHz, and each new shot restarts it.
- **Death:** 56 frames of low noise, starting two frames after the death.
- **March:** a tone of about 7 frames every 16 frames, on frames 1 more than a multiple of 16. It is silent while no segment is alive. Two kinds of beat alternate, and what picks each is unknown.

**Calls I made** (all in `docs/decisions.md`):
- The manifest lives at `assets/sounds/<game>.txt`. Each sound says original or ours; an original adds its file, replay, frame window and a hash of what made it.
- `amb-render` plays sound, never `amb-core`. The cues only read the core's state.
- Each clip's window starts at the end of the frame whose step fires its cue, so the original's delay stays inside the clip.
- Each sound gets its own short replay, cut from the start of a stored one.
- The shot sound plays only for a shot that flies. A shot that hits a mushroom on its launch frame never flies, and whether the original sounds for it isn't measured. That case is a new `todo` row, `centiped.sound.shot-blocked`.
- Phase B measurements will follow the format the coordinator pointed me to on `port-precommit-close`: `oracle/sound/<game>/<sound>.txt`, listed by `sound` lines in `oracle/sound/manifest.txt`. None is stored yet.

- cpal 0.18.2 sample conversion and the `StreamConfig` fields: the crate's own source and docs in the cargo registry. This settled the conversion to each device sample format.
- The rest: Rust's standard `sync_channel` and `try_lock`, and our own `regen.rs` for the publish and rollback pattern.

What I found is in `docs/tech-reference.md`. MAME writes mono 16-bit at 192 kHz even with `-sound none`, and when an option is given twice the last value wins. That is why the 192 kHz setting beats the 48 kHz in the shared options.

**Still open on #18:**
- **Phase B, not started:** `sound-measure`, stored measurements, and our own POKEY recreation of the shot.
- **verify and `oracle/sound/`:** verify currently treats any `oracle/` subdirectory as a game. The fix is coming from `port-precommit-close`; adopt it when that branch lands.
- **Other sounds:** the spider, flea, scorpion, extra life, hits, tally, slam and self-test sounds are not isolated. Each needs a replay that brings it on alone.

3. Two follow-up rounds tightened what counts as a cleared wave. Only a shot that takes the last live slot counts (`cleared`). A slot that met the shooter, or slot 11 taken over by the tally's explosion, keeps the same wave (`unshot`).

data.body:
Build Centipede's shots on segments in AvoidMissingBall (~/GitHub/avoidmissingball), issue #1. That means a shot hitting a segment, its split (`centiped.centipede.split`), the head-shot and body-shot scores (`centiped.centipede.head_shot` and its kin), and the mushroom each destroyed segment leaves. Verify feeds these from the trace today, so building them lets verify stop feeding them. Then, if time allows, start the spider (`centiped.spider.*`).

The chain just landed on main c5b3dbc (crates/core/src/centipede.rs). Read its section 25 in docs/games/centiped/oracle-notes.md and its calls in docs/decisions.md. The fresh field landed in 868d816 (lay_field, section 24), and the mushroom field in f64b004 (section 23).

Read first: AGENTS.md (rules and clean-room), playbook/README.md phase 4, docs/games/centiped/facts.md (the facts sheet), docs/games/centiped/mechanics.md, oracle-notes.md, docs/oracle.md, and xtask/src/oracle_check.rs (how verify feeds what isn't built).
- A row is `verified yes` only after sensitivity (nudge each constant; its replay must fail) and coverage.
- Rows whose outcome is fed from the trace stay `no`.
- Numbers come from the stored traces or probe notes, or are entered as `guess` with the probe that would settle them. If you need a new trace, write its replay (the trackball moves fewer than 8 counts a frame) and run `cargo xtask verify --regen --game centiped3 --only <fragment>` under `tools/slot mame 3 --`. Write the probe up in oracle-notes, with each fact marked measured, inferred or unknown, before building on it.
- Read RAM only through mame/cheat.lua, dump.lua and the maps. Never use a disassembly, the ROMs, driver source or the debugger.

Shared files you may change: oracle/centiped3/manifest.txt, mame/maps/centiped3*.lua, new replays and fixtures, crates/core, xtask/src/oracle_check.rs and verify's Centipede keys, the Centipede docs, docs/decisions.md, docs/gaps.md and log/devlog.md. In parallel, a render agent (branch centiped-draw-segments) works only in crates/render, and the POKEY sound branch (pokey-sound) is landing. Your branch lands after pokey-sound. Rebase when main moves.

Rules:
- Work in your own new worktree off main (.claude/worktrees/agent-centiped-hits, branch centiped-hits), with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/agent-centiped-hits. Never edit the shared checkout.
- Run local cargo under `tools/slot cargo 2 --`, and MAME under `tools/slot mame 3 --` with -video none, -window, -nothrottle, fresh cfg and nvram, and SDL_MAC_BACKGROUND_APP=1. Gate with `cargo xtask gate --branch --host studio`.
